open_points.subject: FlowVersion identity for duplicate constants
open_points.text: “Lists whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — … constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)” and “a port with a constant has no other constant” is checked only by the proof.
open_points.question: How are two different constants targeting the same port ordered while computing the identity of the unproven version?
options: Add a value-based tie-breaker to the canonical order
Preserve submission order for tied constants
Refuse duplicate constant destinations before identity is computed
open_points.default_guess: Refuse duplicate constant destinations during composition before computing the identity.

open_points.subject: FlowNode identifiers and flow endpoints
open_points.text: “A flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node” but `node_id` is only required to be “unique within the version.”
open_points.question: May a node have the empty-string identifier, and if so how is it distinguished and ordered against a flow endpoint?
options: Forbid an empty `node_id`
Use a typed endpoint discriminator independent of the string
Allow both and define an additional ordering rule
open_points.default_guess: Forbid an empty `node_id`.

open_points.subject: Port and media-type syntax
open_points.text: A02 requires “a `file` port declares exactly one media type” but gives no accepted media-type grammar, normalization rule, or restrictions on port names, while A09 places port names and media types into multipart headers.
open_points.question: Which port names and media-type strings are valid, and how must quotes, control characters, non-ASCII text and equivalent media-type spellings be handled?
options: Restrict port names and media types to closed ASCII grammars
Define escaping and permit wider Unicode names
Validate media types but separately restrict names used in multipart
open_points.default_guess: Use a conservative ASCII identifier grammar for port names and a parsed, control-free MIME type/subtype grammar for media types.

open_points.subject: TrialCase expected outputs
open_points.text: “its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports” and “every output's digest equals the expected one” do not say whether a present `expected_outputs` map must name every output port exactly once.
open_points.question: Can an authored trial case specify only a subset of expected outputs, an empty expected-output map, or extra output names?
options: Require exactly all output ports when `expected_outputs` is present
Allow a subset and compare only named outputs
Treat an empty map as equivalent to absent
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all output ports when expected outputs are present, and reject extra or missing names.

open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity and evidence
open_points.text: M08 says “a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict,” but its facts include randomly identified `trial_executions`; A04 permits a crash before the verdict and then runs admission afresh, producing different TrialExecution identities.
open_points.question: Are TrialExecution references part of an AdmissionVerdict's value identity, and what happens to executions left by an interrupted admission?
options: Identify a verdict only by implementation and corpus, treating execution references as attached evidence
Include execution references and allow historically different verdict values for the same pair
Reuse the interrupted admission's executions instead of rerunning
open_points.default_guess: Identify the verdict by implementation and corpus and treat the particular execution references as evidence rather than identity facts.

open_points.subject: Deterministic function execution
open_points.text: K-05 calls admission deterministic and A03 tests that the same implementation and input produce the same digest, but the closed traps still allow sources such as process IDs, object identities, runtime-file metadata and other OS observations.
open_points.question: Which observable Python and operating-system sources must be fixed or denied so deterministic execution is actually guaranteed?
options: Close and enforce a complete deterministic-runtime interface
Permit remaining nondeterminism and define admission as deterministic only for one observed execution set
Run cases repeatedly and reject differing outputs
open_points.default_guess: Expose a closed deterministic interface and deny OS observations not explicitly allowed.

open_points.subject: Function filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input,” while A03 mounts a read-only runtime and an exchange directory and permits opening paths inside both.
open_points.question: May agent code directly read runtime files or create arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or may only the trusted runner access those paths?
options: Deny user-code filesystem calls entirely
Allow reads of the runtime and reads/writes in the exchange directory
Expose only explicitly named input and output files
open_points.default_guess: Allow only runner-mediated input and output files, denying arbitrary user-code filesystem access.

open_points.subject: Sandbox runtime contents
open_points.text: A03 specifies “a read-only runtime” and “its standard library and nothing else” without defining the files, native libraries, executables or metadata included in that runtime.
open_points.question: What exact runtime image is mounted, and which executables and native modules are reachable by function code?
options: A release-built minimal runtime manifest
The host CPython installation
A container or filesystem image pinned by digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-built minimal runtime image pinned by content digest.

open_points.subject: ResourceBounds enforcement
open_points.text: Resource bounds name `memory_bytes` and `process_count`, and A03 says they are enforced with `setrlimit`, but does not define what is counted, whether the runner counts, or how simultaneous limit signals are attributed.
open_points.question: What exact resources count toward memory and process limits, and when is a limit considered hit?
options: Count the whole sandbox including its runner and all descendants
Count only user-code descendants
Define limits by the precise operating-system rlimit semantics
open_points.default_guess: Count the entire sandbox process tree, including the runner, using explicitly documented OS metrics.

open_points.subject: Sandbox cleanup confirmation
open_points.text: “If that cannot be confirmed” the execution becomes `cleanup_failed` and the kernel stops, but confirmation and its deadline are not defined.
open_points.question: Which reap or removal results constitute confirmed cleanup, how long may cleanup take, and which errors trigger kernel termination?
options: Require all process waits and recursive deletion to succeed before a fixed deadline
Treat absence of live processes as sufficient even if files remain
Retry cleanup until success without a separate deadline
open_points.default_guess: Require all processes reaped and the exchange directory removed within a fixed release-defined cleanup deadline.

open_points.subject: Sandbox dependency and probe closure
open_points.text: A20 says a release “pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of the sandbox runtime,” while the texts name neither those dependencies nor their versions, and A03 only requires that “one probe execution succeeds.”
open_points.question: Which dependencies and versions form release v1, which Bubblewrap version or capability set is required, and what must the startup probe demonstrate?
options: Specify an exact lockfile, runtime image and capability probe
Allow any compatible dependency versions and Bubblewrap
Pin only Python while probing host isolation features dynamically
open_points.default_guess: Pin an exact dependency lock and runtime image, and probe every isolation property A03 relies on.

open_points.subject: Guard value comparison
open_points.text: A13 says a guarded edge delivers when the guard port's value “equals its guard value,” without defining equality for JSON numbers, strings, arrays or objects.
open_points.question: What equality relation decides a guard match?
options: Equality of canonical JSON bytes
JSON data-model equality with numeric equivalence
Schema-enumeration member identity
open_points.default_guess: Compare canonical JSON bytes.

open_points.subject: OperationBinding port validation
open_points.text: A08 refuses ports that “break a rule A02 sets for contract ports — unique names per direction, a media type exactly on `file` ports — or leave out the class M01 requires,” but A02 also requires supported schemas, classes only on inputs and at least one output, some of which conflict with binding rules allowing classified outputs and no outputs.
open_points.question: Exactly which A02 port rules apply to bindings, in what order, and are binding schemas validated against the supported schema subset before A09 inspects their `type`?
options: List a separate complete binding-port validation sequence
Apply all A02 rules except explicitly enumerated exceptions
Apply only the two A02 rules named in A08
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate complete binding validation sequence, including supported-schema validation and explicit binding-specific class and output rules.

open_points.subject: Manifest record schema
open_points.text: A08 names some missing fields and invalid values but does not define the full shapes and types of `capabilities`, capability entries, `exposed_as`, `idempotency_key`, instances or `required_headers`.
open_points.question: How are malformed manifest structures not explicitly listed classified and ordered against the listed manifest-mismatch checks?
options: Validate against a complete closed manifest schema first
Treat each malformed shape as the nearest listed missing or invalid condition
Let the manifest reader reject them as generic invalid JSON or manifest mismatch
open_points.default_guess: Validate against a complete closed manifest schema with a specified field-by-field failure order.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision access
open_points.text: The kernel reads `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` “at the configured `manifest_revision`,” but the text does not say how a revision is resolved, snapshotted or protected from working-tree changes.
open_points.question: What storage or repository mechanism supplies a file at `manifest_revision`, and what happens when that revision is absent or changes during a read?
options: Read immutable Git objects at an exact commit
Treat `manifest_location` as an immutable revision directory
Read the live filesystem and use the revision only as metadata
open_points.default_guess: Resolve an exact immutable Git commit and read the blob from that commit.

open_points.subject: Idempotency-key digest construction
open_points.text: The key is “the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of those fields' values,” but no enclosing JSON shape is specified for multiple fields.
open_points.question: Is the canonical JSON hashed as an ordered array, an object keyed by field name, or separate field/value tuples, and how is an explicitly declared empty field list represented?
options: Object keyed by field names
Array of values in manifest order
Array of name/value pairs in manifest order
open_points.default_guess: Hash an array of name/value pairs in manifest order.

open_points.subject: Service base URL
open_points.text: A08 accepts an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host, and A09 forms the target from the base “without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path.” It does not address user information, query, fragment, base paths, percent escapes, ports or multiple trailing slashes.
open_points.question: Which URL components are permitted in `api_base_url`, and what exact join and normalization algorithm is used?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port
Allow a path prefix but forbid user information, query and fragment
Use a standard URL resolver with its normalization behavior
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme, host, optional port and a normalized path prefix; forbid user information, query and fragment; define concatenation without URL resolution.

open_points.subject: Path placeholder serialization
open_points.text: Placeholder values may be strings or integers and are “percent-encoded,” but integer lexical form and handling of already escaped text are not stated.
open_points.question: What exact bytes are percent-encoded for path integers and strings?
options: Canonical-JSON lexical form for integers and UTF-8 string contents
Language-native string conversion
Require all placeholder values to be strings
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical-JSON integer spelling and UTF-8 bytes of the unescaped string value, then percent-encode once.

open_points.subject: Multipart request encoding
open_points.text: A09 specifies parts and headers but not boundary generation, CRLF framing, quoting or escaping of names and filenames, nor treatment of non-ASCII header parameters.
open_points.question: What exact multipart wire encoding must the invoker produce, especially for port names containing quotes, backslashes, controls or non-ASCII characters?
options: Restrict names so no escaping is needed and define exact CRLF framing
Define RFC-compliant escaping and extended parameters
Delegate multipart serialization to the chosen HTTP library
open_points.default_guess: Restrict names to a safe ASCII grammar and define an exact multipart framing algorithm.

open_points.subject: Outbound service-request size
open_points.text: A20 says over a ceiling for “requests” is refused, but only `surface_request_bytes_max` is defined; no aggregate ceiling is given for a generated HTTP request or persisted approval preview.
open_points.question: What bounds the full outbound URL, headers, JSON or multipart body and approval preview, including repeated references to the same large file?
options: Add an explicit outbound-request ceiling
Use `surface_request_bytes_max` for outbound requests too
Rely only on per-value, per-file and spool limits
open_points.default_guess: Add a release-defined aggregate outbound-request and preview ceiling checked before approval is requested.

open_points.subject: Interrupted HTTP response body
open_points.text: A09 distinguishes “no valid final response received” from a “status 2xx” whose outputs fail, but does not classify a timeout, reset, premature EOF or malformed chunking after a final 2xx status and headers have arrived but before its body is complete.
open_points.question: Does an incomplete 2xx response make a non-read attempt `unknown`, or `applied` with `contract_violation`; and how are analogous incomplete 3xx, 4xx and 5xx bodies classified?
options: A response is final only after its complete framed body arrives
The final status decides effect outcome even if its body is incomplete
Use status for 3xx/4xx/5xx but require a complete body for 2xx
open_points.default_guess: Use status for 3xx, 4xx and 5xx as soon as final headers are valid, but treat an incomplete 2xx response as `unknown` for non-read operations.

open_points.subject: Plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: Plain HTTP is allowed when the `api_base_url` host “is a loopback address,” without saying whether hostnames are resolved, which textual IPv4 and IPv6 forms count, or whether every resolved address must be loopback.
open_points.question: How is the loopback exception determined and protected against DNS rebinding?
options: Require a literal loopback IP address
Resolve the hostname and require every result to be loopback
Accept `localhost` and literal loopback forms
open_points.default_guess: Require a canonical literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback address.

open_points.subject: TLS verification
open_points.text: A09 states only “TLS is verified for `https`.”
open_points.question: Which trust roots, hostname rules, minimum TLS versions and certificate policies define successful verification?
options: Use a release-pinned CA bundle and TLS policy
Use the host operating system's default trust and TLS policy
Make trust policy installation configuration
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-pinned CA bundle and an explicit minimum TLS version and hostname-verification policy.

open_points.subject: Credential text decoding
open_points.text: A17 removes “one trailing newline” and refuses an empty value or “a control character,” without defining newline form, multiple terminal newlines or the control-character set.
open_points.question: Does the kernel remove LF, CRLF or either; exactly one sequence or all trailing sequences; and which Unicode or byte values count as control characters?
options: Remove exactly one terminal LF, accepting an optional preceding CR, then reject all remaining C0/C1 controls
Remove all trailing line endings
Remove only one byte `0A` and reject ASCII C0 controls
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one terminal LF with an optional preceding CR, then reject all remaining Unicode control characters.

open_points.subject: EffectApproval attempt number after `not_sent`
open_points.text: M24 says an approval's `attempt_number` is “the number of the attempt it was requested for,” while M26/A14 keep an approval unused after a `not_sent` attempt and use it for a new attempt on resume; A11 says every new NodeExecution takes the next attempt number.
open_points.question: When approval requested for attempt 1 survives a `not_sent` attempt and authorizes attempt 2, what does its immutable `attempt_number` mean and is that cross-attempt use valid?
options: Keep the original requested-for number and explicitly allow it to authorize a later retry
Do not consume an attempt number for `not_sent`
Create a new approval record for the resumed attempt
open_points.default_guess: Keep the original number as historical request context and explicitly permit that approval to authorize the next attempt after `not_sent`.

open_points.subject: StandingGrant after revocation
open_points.text: M25 allows only `active` → `revoked`; A10 says granting an already active node returns the grant but does not say whether a revoked node can be granted again.
open_points.question: Can the owner grant the same node again after revocation, and if so is that a new grant or reactivation of the old record?
options: Create a new grant entity
Reactivate the revoked grant
Refuse all later grants for that node and version
open_points.default_guess: Allow it by creating a new grant entity, leaving the revoked record unchanged.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution facts for non-executed conclusions
open_points.text: A15 requires records for `skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed` and owner refusal, but only says `executed` is absent for the first two; it does not fix their input references, `started_at`, `ended_at`, resources or failure detail.
open_points.question: What exact NodeExecution fields and timestamps are recorded for skipped, upstream-failed, receiving-side contract violations and owner-refused elements?
options: Define a complete status-by-status field matrix
Record only identity, status and one timestamp for non-executed records
Populate all currently available inputs and use the decision/check time for both timestamps
open_points.default_guess: Define a status-by-status matrix; record available inputs, no outputs or resources, and use the conclusion time for both timestamps when execution never started.

open_points.subject: Mapped aggregate output failure
open_points.text: A13 says an oversized mapped value list is not written and the node is failed, while “only a list that is delivered … is measured”; it does not specify output-port or edge delivery order when a mapped node has several outputs and only one aggregate is oversized.
open_points.question: Are all mapped outputs assembled and validated atomically before any is delivered, or can earlier valid outputs be delivered before a later aggregate fails; and in what order are outputs checked?
options: Validate every aggregate first and deliver none if any fails
Check ports in name order and keep earlier deliveries
Fail only dependants of the oversized output
open_points.default_guess: Assemble and validate all mapped outputs atomically in port-name order, and deliver none if any aggregate is too large.

open_points.subject: Startup check precedence
open_points.text: A03, A09, A16, A17 and A18 each add conditions that refuse kernel startup, but no global order says which failure is reported when several conditions fail.
open_points.question: In what order are configuration-file security, token validation, data-directory checks, manifest/header collisions, dependency checks, sandbox probing and recovery performed?
options: Specify one global startup phase order
Report all startup failures together
Allow implementation-defined first failure
open_points.default_guess: Specify a fixed global startup phase order and report its first failure.

open_points.subject: Configuration token re-read snapshot
open_points.text: A16 says the kernel reads the file, compares its byte digest and, when it differs, “re-reads it,” without defining whether comparison and parsing use the same byte snapshot or what happens if the file changes between reads.
open_points.question: Which exact file snapshot is validated and installed as the new token list during a concurrent replacement?
options: Read once into bytes and hash and parse those same bytes
Read twice and retry until both digests match
Lock the configuration file while reading
open_points.default_guess: Read one complete byte snapshot and use those same bytes for both digest comparison and parsing.

open_points.subject: Data-directory privacy
open_points.text: A18 says the directory and everything in it are “private to the kernel's user,” unlike A17's explicit rule of no group or other permissions.
open_points.question: Which ownership, file-type and permission-bit conditions are required for the data directory, its parents and every contained file and directory?
options: Require kernel ownership and no group/other permission on every entry
Require only the top-level directory to be mode 0700
Permit stricter ACL-based access checks instead of mode-bit rules
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel ownership and no group/other permissions on the data directory and every contained entry.

open_points.subject: Simultaneous surface requests
open_points.text: A18 says requests are handled “one at a time in the order they arrive,” but does not define arrival order when multiple connections or messages become ready together.
open_points.question: What establishes the total order of concurrent MCP requests?
options: A monotonically assigned receive sequence at complete-message receipt
Transport connection order followed by per-connection message order
Any scheduler order, recorded once selected
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonically increasing sequence when each complete request message is accepted and process that sequence.

open_points.subject: Failed store calls and retained fixture files
open_points.text: K-10 says “The only files the kernel keeps beyond a run are the file fixtures of trial cases,” while A18 permits a failed store call to leave “a published file no record names” and says startup removes temporary files and eligible spools but “nothing else.”
open_points.question: Are unreferenced published value or fixture files garbage-collected, retained forever, or prevented by coordinating publication with the database transaction?
options: Delete unreferenced published files during startup recovery
Retain them permanently as harmless content-addressed orphans
Use a staging protocol so no unreferenced published fixture remains
open_points.default_guess: Remove unreferenced published files during startup recovery after checking all durable references.
